## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Bālovādajātaka* (Ja 246), titled in English as *Foolish Advice*, is a narrative belonging to the Pali Jātaka collection. The opening blurb indicates that the Buddha recounted the story while dwelling in the gabled chamber near Vesālī concerning the general Sīhasenāpati. In secondary scholarship, the Jātaka is noted under the title *Telovado Jātaka* (No. 246) by E. W. Hopkins (1906), who cited it in connection with the justification of eating meat when the consumer harbors no cruel intent [Baba 2012].
